L&T bags ( Significant*) order from 
Noida Metro for Aqua Line Extension 
Mumbai, November 9, 2026: The Heavy Civil Infrastructure business vertical of L&T has 
secured an order from Noida Metro Rail Corporation Ltd for part design and construction of 
the Noida Metro Aqua Line Extension Project.  
The project scope encompasses part design and construction of a 15.1 km elevated viaduct 
from Botanical Garden to Noida Sector-142, and from Depot Station to Boraki. The scope 
includes the construction of 10 elevated metro stations, including architectural finishes. 
Noida Metro Aqua Line Extension is poised to become a landmark urban transit project, 
significantly enhancing regional connectivity and commuter accessibility. The project will 
play a crucial role in supporting Noida's expanding urban landscape and is to be completed 
within a stringent timeline of 36 months.   
About Larsen & Toubro: 
Larsen & Toubro is a USD 32 billion Indian multinational engaged in EPC Projects, Hi-Tech 
Manufacturing, Products and Services, operating across diverse domains and multiple geographies. 
With a strong impetus towards AI & technology, customer–focussed approach and the constant quest 
for top-class quality have enabled L&T to attain and sustain leadership in its major lines of business 
for eight decades.

Moderator:  
Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Thanks for joining the Mphasis Q2FY2027 
Earnings Conference Call. I'm Neerav, your moderator for the day. We have with us 
today, Mr. Nitin Rakesh, CEO of Mphasis; Mr. Aravind Viswanathan, CFO; and Mr. 
Vinay Kalingara, Head of Investor Relations. 
 
As a reminder, there is a webcast link in the call invite email that the Mphasis 
management team will be referring to today. The same presentation is also available on 
the Mphasis website, www.mphasis.com, in the Investors section under Financial and 
Filings as well as both on BSE and NSE websites. I request you to have the presentation 
handy. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero 
on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
Before we begin, I would like to state that some of the statements made in today's 
discussion may be forward-looking in nature and may involve certain risks and 
uncertainties. A detailed statement in this regard is available in the Q2 results release 
that was sent out to all of you earlier. 
 
I now hand over the floor to Mr. Nitin to begin the proceedings of this call. Thank you, 
and over to you, Nitin. 
Nitin Rakesh: 
Thank you, Neerav, and thank you all for joining us today. 
Q2 delivered what we said it would: our strongest sequential growth in three years, broad-
based across verticals and segments. Our pipeline is at a record, and today we are raising 
our growth guidance for the year. I will take you through the numbers, but first, the thesis 
behind them. 
At our Analyst Meet in May, we said the value in enterprise AI is moving from adoption 
to economic outcomes. AI is not only changing how services are delivered; it is changing 
what enterprises buy. Agentic AI asks what systems can do. Enterprise Agency asks what 
the enterprise can now do better. We built Mphasis TriaTM to close what we call the 
Agency Gap: the distance between having AI and having AI make governed decisions 
that move revenue, margin and risk. Five months on, we see three things. 
First, the buyer has changed. Business and operations leaders now fund AI alongside the 
CIO, and their questions are about revenue leakage, planning latency and slow execution, 
not just technology cost. That is where Mphasis ModernizeTM and Mphasis OptimizeTM 
meet them, and where outcome-linked commercial constructs follow. 
Second, Tria works as a closed loop: understand, decide, act, measure and improve, with 
humans governing the exceptions rather than signing off routine work. Every governed 
decision feeds back into the models, so enterprise context compounds. 
Docusign Envelope ID: 783C3A27-8D91-8DBD-8038-5B3411D9F742

 Mphasis Limited 
 
 
November 6, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
 
Third, the moat is not the models. Frontier Models will continue to improve and 
commoditize. Our enduring differentiation lies in understanding enterprise context, 
causal decision intelligence, orchestration and governance, and the organizational 
capability to continuously learn, deploy & scale these capabilities across our client 
enterprises. 
Independent research points the same way. ISG's September report, ‘The AI Value Gap’, 
found that AI is widely used but outcomes lag, that nearly half of AI budgets now sit 
outside IT, and that model cost is only about a third of total investment. We welcome the 
corroboration, but we did not need it to set our course; it is the course we have been on 
since May, and it is visible in our results. 
What I want to spend time on today is not only what we believe, but how we have 
organized to deliver it. 
Last quarter we said Mphasis Tria was off to a stronger start than we anticipated. In Q2, 
that early traction began to scale. Tria is now a proof point in large-deal evaluations 
because it demonstrates governed, measurable outcomes, not just capability. And it is 
taking us into the operating core of the enterprise: the run of the business, not just the 
technology estate. In BFS, it is opening business-process budgets in lending origination, 
payment exception processing and client onboarding as examples. Beyond BFS, it is 
driving conversations on AI-led operations transformation at large insurers, on-demand 
intelligence for technology clients and so on. These budgets sit with business and 
operations leaders, and this has significantly increased our TAM. 
You will want to know how big our pipeline with Tria is. We are not breaking that out 
today, so let me describe its shape. Tria-led opportunities are a growing part of our 
pipeline, and they are different in kind: larger and multi-year deals, combining 
optimization and transformation with ongoing operations, sponsored by business leaders, 
and increasingly starting with a proof of value on the client's own processes. As each 
first deployment lands, it leaves reusable assets and foundations for expansion within 
that client. 
That brings me to what matters most for execution. We have organized our talent to turn 
this pipeline into scaled delivery. 
• 
Value streams: We have packaged the recurring business problems in Banking, 
Insurance and Healthcare, for example into defined offers, each with a clear buyer, 
outcome measures and reusable assets. Opportunities start from a vertically 
packaged offering. 
• 
Forward deployed and engineering solutions teams sit in one team, alongside 
delivery, embedded within the client, working through four steps: frame the 
problem, compose the capabilities, prove it with evidence, and scale. 
• 
A dedicated product and platform team institutionalizes learnings through a 
continuous feedback loop, turning every deployment into reusable capabilities that 
accelerate the next. 
Docusign Envelope ID: 783C3A27-8D91-8DBD-8038-5B3411D9F742

 Mphasis Limited 
 
 
November 6, 2026 
 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
 
We are investing in people to run this: certifying our client-facing technology leaders on 
the value-stream playbooks and expanding deployment capacity through our FDE team. 
Together, these give us a repeatable path from first conversation to scaled outcome, and 
that is why we are confident in the trajectory. 
Since the launch of Mphasis.ai, three years ago, our pipeline has grown to 3x its original 
size, and AI-led deals have grown from 12% of the pipeline to 71%. 
Net new TCV for Q2 was $466 million. With net new TCV above $400 million for six 
consecutive quarters, we have established a higher baseline for deal closures. That 
baseline supported the growth we delivered in Q2 and underpins our confidence in the 
trajectory for the rest of FY27. 
The pipeline composition is broad-based across verticals and deal sizes. Total pipeline 
reached a new high, growing 4.4% sequentially and 23% YoY. We continue to see a high 
share of proactively originated opportunities, shaped by our point of view on clients’ 
businesses and our ability to identify and define opportunities before they become formal 
asks.  
Growth was broad-based, with the BFS pipeline up 4.1% and the non-BFS pipeline up 
4.8% sequentially. Opportunities below $20 million grew 35% year-on-year and 9% 
sequentially, reflecting the increase in shorter-cycle deal activity we called out last 
quarter, which continues to play out. 
On a year-on-year basis, Modernization and XaaP, now aligned to our Tria product lines, 
recorded the strongest growth in the pipeline. Agile IT Ops and Next Ops are also 
significant contributors to the overall pipeline, reflecting the deals in process 
modernization and business-outcome budgets we described earlier. 
As I mentioned earlier, net new TCV for the quarter was $466 million, with trailing-
twelve-months TCV at $1.8 billion. 66% of our TCV wins in Q2 were AI-led, up from 
63% last quarter. We closed five large deals in Q2. One of them nicely illustrates the 
shift in how the outcome deals are being structured: a large broker-dealer selected 
Mphasis to scale its advisor administration business across front and middle-office 
services. It is a large deal with a recurring revenue-share model and significant expansion 
potential across the client's advisor network. 
Deal wins continue to convert to revenue at a consistent pace. As we said last quarter, 
the trend of shorter-cycle deals is holding, with TCV for deals below $20 million up 26% 
on a TTM basis. Meanwhile, the backlog we built over prior quarters and the steady TCV 
wins provides ongoing support to in-quarter and near-term revenue conversion as well. 
Moving to our segment performance. In the Direct business, we grew 3.5% sequentially 
and 11.3% year-over-year in constant currency terms. 
From a geographic perspective, Americas continued to be our primary growth engine. It 
grew 3.1% sequentially and 12.4% YoY in Direct, driven by ramp-ups in large deal wins 
Docusign Envelope ID: 783C3A27-8D91-8DBD-8038-5B3411D9F742

November 6, 2026 
 
 
Page 5 of 18 
 
 
and contributions from new logos. The Rest of the World delivered strong growth of 
16.4% sequentially and 23.5% YoY in constant currency terms. This was led by our 
growing participation in the GCC ecosystem with our global clients. EMEA declined 
3.3% sequentially and 9.0% YoY. As we have explained before, we classify geographies 
by the origin of contract. This quarter's EMEA numbers reflect revenue from a globally 
structured engagement that was allocated across regions. The underlying health of the 
business there remains intact. 
From a service line perspective, Enterprise Applications remains our core growth engine 
and contributed to 75.6% of our revenue. Direct revenue grew 3.7% sequentially and 
14.4% YoY in constant currency, driven predominantly by AI-led modernization deals. 
BPO sustained its momentum, growing 6.6% sequentially and 18.7% YoY in Direct on 
new deal wins and AI-led propositions. Tria-led process modernization has become a 
defining theme in business reimagination since launch, driving pipeline and wins across 
APPS and BPO. 
ITO declined 4.9% sequentially and 21.3% YoY. This mainly reflects transformation 
projects moving into a steady phase. These were integrated build-plus-run programs, and, 
as the build components finish, the work moves into the run phase. This impact is also 
reflected in the Others vertical. 
Moving to performance by vertical, BFS Direct grew 4.5% sequentially and 15.0% YoY 
in constant currency, with an eight-quarter CQGR of 3.8%. Growth continues to come 
from wallet share gains in existing accounts and new deal wins, reflecting our domain 
depth and right to win in Financial Services. 
Insurance returned to sequential growth of 1.8% and grew 14.7% YoY in Direct, 
supported by Tria-led optimization programs across underwriting, claims and risk 
operations. Based on last quarter's recovery and new deal ramp ups, TMT grew 10.9% 
sequentially and 14.5% YoY in Direct. 
On a TTM basis, BFS, Insurance and TMT, the verticals we identified as growth drivers, 
have all delivered, showing that our strategic focus is translating into results. In Direct - 
BFS, Insurance and TMT delivered 15%, 28% and 12% growth respectively on a TTM 
basis. 
Logistics and Transportation declined 12.0% sequentially, on a smaller base. It continues 
to feel some impact from ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. It is now a smaller unit for 
us, so small changes in revenue produce larger percentage swings. While the Others 
segment declined 6.4% sequentially and grew 1.8% YoY, Healthcare within that segment 
delivered healthy growth. On the back of recent deal wins, including a large deal win this 
quarter, we expect Healthcare to emerge as a growth driver. 
Moving on to client metrics, they show growth across the portfolio. On a TTM basis, our 
Top 5 clients grew 15.1% YoY, and our Top 10 grew 13.0% YoY. Our Top 11–20 clients 
grew faster, at 22.7% YoY. That reflects the investment we made to widen our account 
Docusign Envelope ID: 783C3A27-8D91-8DBD-8038-5B3411D9F742

 Mphasis Limited 
 
 
November 6, 2026 
 
 
Page 6 of 18 
 
 
coverage from the top 10 to the next 20. Sequentially, the Top 5 grew 4.1% and clients 
ranked 6–10 grew 4.9%. This growth has been driven largely by strong in-account 
execution - winning new deals and ramping them up. 
Our client buckets are aligned the same way. We added two clients in the $50 million-
plus bracket sequentially, three in the $20 million-plus bracket year-on-year, and five in 
the $5 million-plus bracket year-on-year, three of them on a sequential basis as well. As 
new accounts scale, they keep feeding the upper tiers of the pyramid. 
Moving to our financial metrics performance. Q2 EBIT margin remained flat. EPS 
increased 14.6% sequentially to INR 29.4. Operating Cash flow generation was USD 
34Mn after normalizing USD 39.5Mn of remittances initiated on 30th September and 
received in October. 
DSO for the quarter was 105 days after normalizing for the delayed remittances I just 
mentioned on the previous slide. This is more of a quarterly aberration and is expected 
to get to double digit levels in Q3. 
In summary: in July we said Q2 would deliver our best sequential constant-currency 
growth in three years, and that it would be broad-based and it did.  
Direct revenue grew 3.5% sequentially and 11.3% year-on-year. BFS grew 4.5% 
sequentially and 15.0% year-on-year, and TMT grew 10.9% sequentially. The Americas 
and the Rest of the World delivered strong sequential growth. Applications and BPO 
were driven by AI-led modernization and new deal wins. Our Top 5 clients grew 15.1% 
year-on-year, and our Top 11 to 20 grew 22.7%, with additions across client bands, both 
sequentially and year-on-year. 
The pipeline is at a record, up 23% year-on-year, with 71% of the pipeline being AI-led, 
and it spans verticals, deal sizes and archetypes. TCV wins were $466 million for the 
quarter, 66% AI-led, including five large deals, taking trailing-twelve-month TCV to 
$1.8 billion. And we delivered stable margins within our stated range. 
That performance, and the visibility behind it, is why we are raising our outlook. Let me 
turn to how we see the rest of the year. 
The first half has set a strong foundation for FY27, and we expect the second half to 
carry this momentum forward. Four things give us that confidence: a record and broad-
based pipeline; six consecutive quarters of net new TCV above $400 million, with the 
backlog converting to revenue; steady execution from signing to revenue; and an 
organization built to scale the work we are winning. 
On that basis, we are raising our FY27 guidance. We now expect revenue growth in the 
low double digits for the full year. Last quarter, our guidance was high single digits to 
low double digits. We are doing so despite an uncertain macro environment, because it 
rests on results already delivered and on visibility we can see in the pipeline and the 
backlog. 
Docusign Envelope ID: 783C3A27-8D91-8DBD-8038-5B3411D9F742

 Mphasis Limited 
 
 
November 6, 2026 
 
 
Page 7 of 18 
 
 
On profitability, we continue to expect stable margins within the target band of 14.75% 
to 15.75%, while we invest in the capabilities that drive the next phase of growth. We 
continue to target 80% conversion of net income to operating cash flow in FY27, further 
normalizing in FY28.  
With that, I will open the call for questions. Operator, over to you. 
 
Moderator:  
First question is from the line of Gaurav Rateria from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead. 
Gaurav, may I request to unmute your line and proceed with your question, please? 
Gaurav Rateria: 
Hi. Congrats on good revenue performance. I have three questions. My first question is 
on your confidence for upgrading the guidance in the current macro. And the reason I'm 
asking is because your deal wins have been in that particular range, so within the same 
deal win range, why upgrade of guidance or giving more confidence on the second half? 
So, is that conversion ratio improving versus the past? Is that giving you more 
confidence? 
My second question is on pipeline. Historically, we have seen, Nitin, that pipeline has 
been a lead indicator for your deal win numbers to inch up. You started building on 
pipeline and deal win numbers eventually started to inch up with a lag. Now, given that 
the pipeline is building up now, is it fair to say that some of that will start reflecting in 
step up in the deal win numbers over a period of next two or three quarters? 
And the last question is that where are we in the investment cycle on building these IPs 
and deal archetype that we had talked about on Tria and other things? At some point in 
time, will that investment phase plateau out and will that lead to margin accretion for the 
company as a whole? Thank you. 
Nitin Rakesh: 
Thanks, Gaurav. I think the upgrade question linked to TCV, let me take it in two 
different ways. As I mentioned in my script, the confidence is really coming from what 
we have in the backlog combined with the pipeline and the deal propensity. And of 
course, we've added some healthy revenue in-quarter in Q2 that gives us a starting base 
from a run rate perspective. That is also reflected in the client addition, especially when 
you see the client metrics of top five, top 10 and next 10. I think all of those metrics are 
green. So, there's a fair amount of that run rate confidence that's coming in. 
On the question around linking it to TCV, while the TCV has stayed in the $400 million 
range, this is still a little bit higher than what we've had in the last three or four quarters, 
as I mentioned in the commentary itself, it's not just the TCV that matters. The shape and 
nature of the TCV matters as well when it comes to short-term growth and revenue 
performance. 
As I mentioned, if you look at just the trailing 12 months, there's a 26% increase in small 
deal TCV. Even if you look at the pipeline, we've seen a disproportionate increase in the 
less than $20 million TCV in the pipeline at 35%, when the overall pipeline is up about

 Mphasis Limited 
 
 
November 6, 2026

23%. So, what's happening is a fair amount of work and priority from clients is focused 
on three areas right now.  
First is all AI engineering work. Almost every large enterprise is very rapidly focused on 
building the AI foundations, the AI harness, the AI infrastructure layer that will 
effectively enable them to adopt AI at scale, and that's leading to a fair amount of work 
in aligning and helping them design, build, deploy, and scale these harnesses and 
foundations. Tria plays a role there as well because in many cases there's an opportunity 
for us to help them expand their thinking on what the foundation should look like. So 
that's the first bucket of work. Again, corroborated by headcount addition and growth in 
applications and growth in top accounts. Not a phenomenon that's happening across client 
segments, but definitely the more mature, the larger clients are spending a fair amount of 
time, effort, and money. And these are typically the short-cycle deals. So, I'll give you 
an example. A $10 million, six-month deal has the same propensity as a $100 million, 
five-year deal when it comes to revenue growth.  
Second thing that is in focus is kind of linked to the first one, is the whole investment 
that is going into hardening the cyber estate. Also, fairly AI engineering led because it 
isn't just about adopting a new AI tool or AI platform. It's also about hardening the way

going on in the client side, and that's what's driving the pipeline and the TCV wins, but

to obviously keep the conversion rate as high as it is or higher, and hence that will reflect

humans governing the exceptions rather than signing off routine work. Every governed 
decision feeds back into the models, so enterprise context compounds.

you idea about the results yesterday.

INR5,539 crores, highest ever PBT of INR5,160 crores, highest ever PAT of INR3,837 crores. 
The H1 net profit was up by 54% year-on-year basis compared to INR3,837 crores of last year 
'25-26’.  The Q2 net profit, of Rs.1,835 up by 28% year-on-year basis. 
So without waiting any time, we open the floor for question answers from our side and our CMD 
Shri Brijendra Pratap Singh sir will address all the queries raised by the team members attending 
this conference call. Thank you.

question is from the line of Manav Gogia from Aditya Birla Institutional Equities. Please go 
ahead.

around what's the status on the refinery? And if you could just elaborate on where we are 
currently in terms of commissioning and the stabilization? And along with this, if you could also

November 03, 2026

the refinery, Pottangi and Utkal. Myself BP Singh CMD, NALCO. Refinery, 5th Stream refinery

packages. We have completed and started the trials testing.

completed. Three, four packages are in the critical path, which are already almost 90% 
completion. Physical completion, 90%, 92% physical completion is there. So what we are 
targeting is the packages which are getting completed.

trial of the 5th Stream and start of the production, we have planned in last quarter -- last month, 
last week of the December. Maybe we will be completing all the packages which is left out and 
starting the integrated trial and starting the production from last week of December or maybe 
early of January. So that is the status of 5th Stream refinery.

signed, EGA in Dubai, they will be giving the technology that was signed two months back.

first quarter, we'll start the commissioning. So, till now, the timelines we are maintaining.

already -- we are making a JV company with Neyveli Lignite Corporation. Neyveli Lignite 
Corporation, 50% -- 50% JV company is already approved by DIPAM and all that. We are

Crude Tankers
•
Global crude trade recovered 8% q/q, with AG loadings improving to ~60% of pre-war levels in Q2 
FY27. AG loadings rose to ~8 mbpd in Q2 FY27 and remain on an upward trend; however, 
sustainability remains a key risk given the escalation in Iranian attacks.
•
Transits through Hormuz remains inefficient, resulting in longer voyage times.
•
China’s seaborne crude imports improved sequentially to ~7.4 mbpd, although volumes remain ~3–4 
mbpd below pre-war levels.
•
West of Suez loadings remain elevated. In addition, the rerouting of cargoes due to the Yanbu 
disruption further supported ton-miles.
•
The total crude tanker fleet grew by ~2% y/y; however, inefficient STS operations in the AG, higher 
West-to-East flows and the rerouting of Yanbu cargoes have kept the fleet stretched.
Product Tankers
•
Global product trade improved 9% q/q in Q2 FY27, driven by a recovery in exports from Asia and the 
Middle East. Refinery throughput also improved q/q, supported by strong margins and better crude 
availability.
•
AG CPP exports have improved to ~40% of pre-war levels in Q2 FY27 but diesel market remains acutely 
tight, with minimal Russian exports. 
•
Asian exports to the west rebounded in Q2 FY27, taking advantage of the strong diesel cracks in the 
West. 
•
The total product tanker fleet grew by ~6% y/y. However, the LR2 fleet has contracted by 30% y/y, 
primarily due to vessels switching to dirty trades.
Tanker asset prices & order book
•
Suezmax tanker prices have risen 50–55% q/q, while Aframax and product tanker prices have increased 
by 10–20%.
•
The order book for crude and product tankers stands at 28% and 22% of the respective fleets.

The strength in bulk carrier earnings continued through Q2 FY27. Capesize earnings outperformed, 
rising 67% y/y, while Kamsarmax and Supramax earnings each grew y/y by 27%. 
Capesizes were supported by a ramp-up in iron ore exports from the Simandou project in Guinea 
along with strong Guinean bauxite exports which grew by ~35% y/y during the quarter.
After rising ~8% y/y in the previous quarter, coal trade retreated by 4% y/y during Q2 FY27. China’s 
electricity demand was met by rising Renewables and Hydro powered generation, keeping coal import 
requirement in check. India’s coal import demand also remained weak due to higher prices and 
continued inventory drawdown.
Grain trade softened by ~6% y/y during the quarter as intensifying attacks hampered flow of 
Russian and Ukrainian grains from the Black Sea Region. 
Bulk Carrier asset prices rose between 5% and 10% q/q during Q2 FY27, depending on vessel type 
and age profile.
Bulk carrier fleet grew by 3% y/y during Q2 FY27.
Orderbook-to-fleet for the dry bulk sector stands at ~16% of fleet.

VLGC spot earnings surged 135% y/y in Q2 FY27. 
Overall trade volumes declined by 14% y/y as MEG exports halved. However, share of 
ship-to-ship transfers in total exports via Hormuz jumped to ~75% in Q2 FY27 , creating 
artificial inefficiencies and lending support to the market.
High Panama Canal fees pushed more ships via the Cape of Good Hope thereby further 
supporting the tonne-miles.
Normalized US terminal fees allowed freight to capture a wider share of the US–Far East 
arbitrage, which remained supportive due to strong Asian demand and high US 
inventories.
VLGC fleet supply grew 8% y/y in Q2 FY27. 
Asset values continue to trend higher, now up 18% q/q. 
The total VLGC orderbook-to-fleet ratio remains elevated at 39% amidst higher contracting.

Crude Tankers
•
Global crude trade recovered 8% q/q, with AG loadings improving to ~60% of pre-war levels in Q2 
FY27. AG loadings rose to ~8 mbpd in Q2 FY27 and remain on an upward trend; however, 
sustainability remains a key risk given the escalation in Iranian attacks.
•
Transits through Hormuz remains inefficient, resulting in longer voyage times.
•
China’s seaborne crude imports improved sequentially to ~7.4 mbpd, although volumes remain ~3–4 
mbpd below pre-war levels.
•
West of Suez loadings remain elevated. In addition, the rerouting of cargoes due to the Yanbu 
disruption further supported ton-miles.
•
The total crude tanker fleet grew by ~2% y/y; however, inefficient STS operations in the AG, higher 
West-to-East flows and the rerouting of Yanbu cargoes have kept the fleet stretched.
Product Tankers
•
Global product trade improved 9% q/q in Q2 FY27, driven by a recovery in exports from Asia and the 
Middle East. Refinery throughput also improved q/q, supported by strong margins and better crude 
availability.
•
AG CPP exports have improved to ~40% of pre-war levels in Q2 FY27 but diesel market remains acutely 
tight, with minimal Russian exports. 
•
Asian exports to the west rebounded in Q2 FY27, taking advantage of the strong diesel cracks in the 
West. 
•
The total product tanker fleet grew by ~6% y/y. However, the LR2 fleet has contracted by 30% y/y, 
primarily due to vessels switching to dirty trades.
Tanker asset prices & order book
•
Suezmax tanker prices have risen 50–55% q/q, while Aframax and product tanker prices have increased 
by 10–20%.
•
The order book for crude and product tankers stands at 28% and 22% of the respective fleets.

The strength in bulk carrier earnings continued through Q2 FY27. Capesize earnings outperformed, 
rising 67% y/y, while Kamsarmax and Supramax earnings each grew y/y by 27%. 
Capesizes were supported by a ramp-up in iron ore exports from the Simandou project in Guinea 
along with strong Guinean bauxite exports which grew by ~35% y/y during the quarter.
After rising ~8% y/y in the previous quarter, coal trade retreated by 4% y/y during Q2 FY27. China’s 
electricity demand was met by rising Renewables and Hydro powered generation, keeping coal import 
requirement in check. India’s coal import demand also remained weak due to higher prices and 
continued inventory drawdown.
Grain trade softened by ~6% y/y during the quarter as intensifying attacks hampered flow of 
Russian and Ukrainian grains from the Black Sea Region. 
Bulk Carrier asset prices rose between 5% and 10% q/q during Q2 FY27, depending on vessel type 
and age profile.
Bulk carrier fleet grew by 3% y/y during Q2 FY27.
Orderbook-to-fleet for the dry bulk sector stands at ~16% of fleet.

VLGC spot earnings surged 135% y/y in Q2 FY27. 
Overall trade volumes declined by 14% y/y as MEG exports halved. However, share of 
ship-to-ship transfers in total exports via Hormuz jumped to ~75% in Q2 FY27 , creating 
artificial inefficiencies and lending support to the market.
High Panama Canal fees pushed more ships via the Cape of Good Hope thereby further 
supporting the tonne-miles.
Normalized US terminal fees allowed freight to capture a wider share of the US–Far East 
arbitrage, which remained supportive due to strong Asian demand and high US 
inventories.
VLGC fleet supply grew 8% y/y in Q2 FY27. 
Asset values continue to trend higher, now up 18% q/q. 
The total VLGC orderbook-to-fleet ratio remains elevated at 39% amidst higher contracting.

PRESS RELEASE 
 
Shyam Metalics Reaffirms Credit Ratings of ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and ‘CRISIL A1+’; Bank 
Debt Ratings Enhanced to ₹4,500 Crore 
 
Kolkata, November 09, 2026 — Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (SMEL), one of India’s leading 
integrated multi-metal producing companies, announced today that CRISIL Ratings Limited has reaffirmed 
the company’s long-term rating at ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and short-term rating at ‘CRISIL A1+’. CRISIL 
has enhanced the rated bank debt amount to ₹4,500 Crore (up from ₹3,600 Crore), and reaffirmed the rating 
for its ₹50 Crore Commercial Paper programme at ‘CRISIL A1+’.  
 
The reaffirmation underscores the Shyam Metalics Group’s established market position in the steel sector, 
strong financial risk profile, healthy operating performance, and high operational efficiency driven by 
deeply integrated operations.  
 
Key Highlights Driving the Rating Reaffirmation 
 
 
Robust Operating Performance & Growth: Operating profitability and top-line growth continue 
to strengthen, supported by higher sales volumes across core product segments. Profitability 
metrics are projected to expand further in the upcoming fiscal year.  
 
 
Capacity Expansion & Diversification: The group continues to scale its aggregate production 
capacities. Strategic expansion into flat steel, pig iron, stainless steel, and aluminium foils 
reinforces its product diversification and market reach.  
 
 
Integrated Value Chain & Efficiency: Operations cover the complete value chain from raw 
materials to value-added finished products. Operational efficiency is heavily supported by captive 
power generation, waste heat recovery plants, coal washeries, and dedicated railway sidings. 
Planned coal block operationalization will further strengthen long-term energy and raw material 
security.  
 
 
Strong Balance Sheet & Conservative Leverage: The group maintains a conservative financial 
structure with a strong net worth, significant liquidity surplus, and minimal debt reliance, leading 
to low gearing and strong interest coverage.  
 
 
Disciplined Funding of Growth Capex: Multi-year capital expenditure plans for capacity 
expansion will be funded predominantly through strong annual internal accruals and available cash 
reserves, ensuring debt metrics remain at safe levels.  
 
 
Commitment to ESG & Sustainability: SMEL continues to advance its environmental goals by 
increasing its renewable energy consumption, maintaining Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) 
operations for full water reuse, and adhering to international standards for emissions reporting.

Management Commentary 
 
"The reaffirmation of our 'CRISIL AA+/Stable' and 'CRISIL A1+' ratings, along with the enhancement of 
our rated bank facilities, validates the strength of our business strategy, robust balance sheet, and disciplined 
execution capabilities. Even as we undertake major brownfield capacity expansions to enhance scale and 
product diversification, our focus remains anchored on prudent capital allocation, maintaining strong 
liquidity, and creating long-term value for all stakeholders." - Mr. Brij Bhushan Agarwal, Chairman & 
Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited 
 
About Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited 
 
Shyam Metalics is a leading and fastest-growing integrated metal-producing company based in India 
primarily in the steel industry in West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Madhya Pradesh with a focus on 
Long & Flat Steel Products, Ferro Alloys, Aluminium, and Stainless Steel. The company got listed itself 
on the exchanges in 2021 and possesses a market capitalization of more than ₹ 35,000 Cr. Headquartered 
in Kolkata, West Bengal, the company is amongst the largest producers of ferro alloys in terms of installed 
capacity in India. 
The company has an aggregate installed metal capacity of 16.93 MTPA across the steel value chain and is 
supported by a 467 MW aggregated installed capacity of captive power plants. For more information, please 
visit our website at https://www.shyammetalics.com/.

PRESS RELEASE 
 
Shyam Metalics Reaffirms Credit Ratings of ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and ‘CRISIL A1+’; Bank 
Debt Ratings Enhanced to ₹4,500 Crore 
 
Kolkata, November 09, 2026 — Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (SMEL), one of India’s leading 
integrated multi-metal producing companies, announced today that CRISIL Ratings Limited has reaffirmed 
the company’s long-term rating at ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and short-term rating at ‘CRISIL A1+’. CRISIL 
has enhanced the rated bank debt amount to ₹4,500 Crore (up from ₹3,600 Crore), and reaffirmed the rating 
for its ₹50 Crore Commercial Paper programme at ‘CRISIL A1+’.  
 
The reaffirmation underscores the Shyam Metalics Group’s established market position in the steel sector, 
strong financial risk profile, healthy operating performance, and high operational efficiency driven by 
deeply integrated operations.  
 
Key Highlights Driving the Rating Reaffirmation 
 
 
Robust Operating Performance & Growth: Operating profitability and top-line growth continue 
to strengthen, supported by higher sales volumes across core product segments. Profitability 
metrics are projected to expand further in the upcoming fiscal year.  
 
 
Capacity Expansion & Diversification: The group continues to scale its aggregate production 
capacities. Strategic expansion into flat steel, pig iron, stainless steel, and aluminium foils 
reinforces its product diversification and market reach.  
 
 
Integrated Value Chain & Efficiency: Operations cover the complete value chain from raw 
materials to value-added finished products. Operational efficiency is heavily supported by captive 
power generation, waste heat recovery plants, coal washeries, and dedicated railway sidings. 
Planned coal block operationalization will further strengthen long-term energy and raw material 
security.  
 
 
Strong Balance Sheet & Conservative Leverage: The group maintains a conservative financial 
structure with a strong net worth, significant liquidity surplus, and minimal debt reliance, leading 
to low gearing and strong interest coverage.  
 
 
Disciplined Funding of Growth Capex: Multi-year capital expenditure plans for capacity 
expansion will be funded predominantly through strong annual internal accruals and available cash 
reserves, ensuring debt metrics remain at safe levels.  
 
 
Commitment to ESG & Sustainability: SMEL continues to advance its environmental goals by 
increasing its renewable energy consumption, maintaining Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) 
operations for full water reuse, and adhering to international standards for emissions reporting.

Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited 
 
About Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited 
 
Shyam Metalics is a leading and fastest-growing integrated metal-producing company based in India 
primarily in the steel industry in West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Madhya Pradesh with a focus on 
Long & Flat Steel Products, Ferro Alloys, Aluminium, and Stainless Steel. The company got listed itself 
on the exchanges in 2021 and possesses a market capitalization of more than ₹ 35,000 Cr. Headquartered 
in Kolkata, West Bengal, the company is amongst the largest producers of ferro alloys in terms of installed 
capacity in India. 
The company has an aggregate installed metal capacity of 16.93 MTPA across the steel value chain and is 
supported by a 467 MW aggregated installed capacity of captive power plants. For more information, please 
visit our website at https://www.shyammetalics.com/.

BlueStone records solid 45% YoY growth in Q3 FY27 (QTD) 
 
November 9, 2026, Bengaluru: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited (‘BlueStone’), a leading digital first, 
direct-to-consumer jewellery brand, is pleased to report provisional business update on its performance for 
quarter till date (QTD: 1-Oct to 8-Nov) of Q3 FY27 over same period last year. 
 
The growth momentum continued into the quarter as the Company recorded a 45% YoY business growth for 
the said period which includes the festive period particularly Dhanteras and Diwali. This growth was largely 
buyer transaction driven with average realisations being the same as last year (comparable period). The 
secular trends towards jewellery for the wardrobe remains intact and this festive our product range across 
entry level price points also saw improved momentum.  
 
Commenting on the performance, BlueStone’s Founder & CEO Gaurav Singh Kushwaha said,  
 
“We continued to build on our strong growth momentum, with robust festive season performance reflecting 
sustained consumer demand and the strength of our business model. Our business grew by 45% over the 
corresponding period last year. It’s exciting to see that growth was fundamentally buyer transaction led. More 
consumers are choosing BlueStone this festive season, reflecting the strength of our design-led proposition 
and our ability to offer differentiated jewellery across a wide range of price points.” 
 
 
Note: All figures are business numbers, interim for the on-going quarter (Q3FY27 QTD), unaudited, and subject to audit review.  
 
About BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited: 
BlueStone is a contemporary lifestyle jewellery brand offering diamond, gold, platinum and studded 
jewellery with a strong design-led approach. Launched in 2011 as a digital-first, direct-to-consumer brand, 
BlueStone has evolved into one of India’s leading omnichannel jewellery retailers with a wide presence 
across the country. The brand retails through its website, mobile app and a growing network of stores, 
providing customers with a seamless online-to-offline experience. With a diverse portfolio spanning rings, 
earrings, necklaces, bangles, solitaires and more, BlueStone caters to modern consumers who value unique 
designs, craftsmanship and innovation across occasions. The Company also operates advanced 
manufacturing facilities to support its expanding scale and product range.

BlueStone records solid 45% YoY growth in Q3 FY27 (QTD) 
 
November 9, 2026, Bengaluru: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited (‘BlueStone’), a leading digital first, 
direct-to-consumer jewellery brand, is pleased to report provisional business update on its performance for 
quarter till date (QTD: 1-Oct to 8-Nov) of Q3 FY27 over same period last year. 
 
The growth momentum continued into the quarter as the Company recorded a 45% YoY business growth for 
the said period which includes the festive period particularly Dhanteras and Diwali. This growth was largely 
buyer transaction driven with average realisations being the same as last year (comparable period). The 
secular trends towards jewellery for the wardrobe remains intact and this festive our product range across 
entry level price points also saw improved momentum.  
 
Commenting on the performance, BlueStone’s Founder & CEO Gaurav Singh Kushwaha said,  
 
“We continued to build on our strong growth momentum, with robust festive season performance reflecting 
sustained consumer demand and the strength of our business model. Our business grew by 45% over the 
corresponding period last year. It’s exciting to see that growth was fundamentally buyer transaction led. More 
consumers are choosing BlueStone this festive season, reflecting the strength of our design-led proposition 
and our ability to offer differentiated jewellery across a wide range of price points.” 
 
 
Note: All figures are business numbers, interim for the on-going quarter (Q3FY27 QTD), unaudited, and subject to audit review.  
 
About BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited: 
BlueStone is a contemporary lifestyle jewellery brand offering diamond, gold, platinum and studded 
jewellery with a strong design-led approach. Launched in 2011 as a digital-first, direct-to-consumer brand, 
BlueStone has evolved into one of India’s leading omnichannel jewellery retailers with a wide presence 
across the country. The brand retails through its website, mobile app and a growing network of stores, 
providing customers with a seamless online-to-offline experience. With a diverse portfolio spanning rings, 
earrings, necklaces, bangles, solitaires and more, BlueStone caters to modern consumers who value unique 
designs, craftsmanship and innovation across occasions. The Company also operates advanced 
manufacturing facilities to support its expanding scale and product range.

HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited 
Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
November 06, 2026 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited 
Earnings Conference Call.   Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the 
conference over to Mr. Anoop Poojari from CDR India.   
Anoop Poojari: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on HealthCare Global 
Enterprises Q2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings conference call. We have with us Dr. Manish Mattoo, 
Executive Director and CEO of the company, Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Chief Financial Officer, and 
Mr. Ravi Gothwal, Head of Investor Relations. We would like to begin the call with opening 
remarks from Manish, following which we will have the forum open for an interactive question-
and-answer session. 
 
Before we start, I would like to point out that some statements made in today's call may be 
forward-looking in nature, and a disclaimer to this effect has been included in the earnings 
presentation shared with you earlier. I would now like to invite Manish to make his opening 
remarks. 
Manish Mattoo: 
Thank you, Anoop. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us for HCG's Quarter 
2 and H1 FY27 earnings call.  
I am pleased to share that we have sustained our growth momentum into the second quarter, 
supported by healthy patient demand and improving revenue mix, and steady progress across 
our strategic and operational priorities. As highlighted in our previous earnings call, our strategic 
priorities remain centered on profitable growth, improving asset utilization, strengthening 
clinical differentiation, and optimizing our revenue mix. 
 
We are encouraged by the progress made during the quarter across all these areas. Coming to 
our financial performance, I would like to highlight that all financial figures presented today 
exclude the Milann Fertility business, which was divested in June 2026. The corresponding 
prior-year figures have also been adjusted accordingly to ensure a like-for-like comparison. 
 
In Quarter 2 FY 2027, HCG delivered revenue of INR 7,318 million, representing a growth of 
16% year- on- year. Revenue growth, excluding our North Bengaluru new hospital, was 14% 

Page 2 of 14 
 
year- on- year. The growth was broad-based across our operating clusters, primarily driven by 
a 9% increase in patient volumes, while average revenue per patient increased by 7% year-on- 
year. 
 
The improvement in ARPP was supported by a favorable payor mix and an increasing 
contribution from high-complexity oncology treatments. This included a 37% year-on-year 
increase in robotic surgeries, alongside growing adoption of other advanced therapies and 
surgical procedures across our network. 
 
As we have consistently emphasized, our objective is not merely to drive higher patient 
volumes, but to enhance the quantity and quality of our revenues through a greater contribution 
from complex oncology procedures and improved payor mix, superior clinical outcomes, and 
higher productivity across our specialized oncology ecosystem. 
 
In line with this strategy, we continue to focus on expanding our non-institutional business while 
progressively optimizing our exposure to lower-realization segments. These efforts are yielding 
encouraging results, with non-institutional revenue growing by 21% year-on-year, resulting in 
an improvement of over 300 basis points in its revenue share to 69%.  
On the profitability front, EBITDA for the quarter, including North Bengaluru loss of INR 61 
million, was INR 1,425 million, representing growth of 17% year-on-year, with EBITDA 
margins improved to 19.7% compared to 19.2% in Q2FY26. 
 
While we continue to benefit from improving revenue quality and operating efficiencies, margin 
expansion during the quarter was partly moderated due to incremental employee cost amounting 
to approximately INR 60 million on account of revision in Karnataka Wage Act 2026. 
 
If you really look at it on a like-to-like basis, excluding the wage revision impact, EBITDA 
growth was over 20% year-on-year. North Bengaluru, our newest hospital, continued to make 
good progress, with its EBITDA loss reducing to INR 61 million during this quarter. Our focus 
remains on accelerating clinical ramp-up, improving capacity utilization, and progressively 
reducing operating losses. 
 
Let me now take you through the performance across our operating clusters.  
Starting with the South cluster, the revenue stood at INR 2,941 million. Delivering a strong 
growth of 18% and contributing to 40% of our overall revenue. Growth was supported by a 14% 
improvement in ARPP and a 4% increase in patient volumes, with a strong contribution from 
our Bengaluru Center of Excellence and the progressive ramp-up of our North Bengaluru 
hospital. 
 
ARPP improvement across the cluster was also aided by a favorable payor mix and higher 
contribution of high-end procedures and therapies.  
Moving to the West cluster. Revenue stood at INR 3,147 million, registering 10% year-on-year 
growth and contributing 43% to overall revenue. Growth was primarily driven by a 7% increase 
in patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 3%, supported by a favorable payor mix. 

Page 3 of 14 
 
 
The Maharashtra region delivered a strong performance with a mid-teens growth, driven by 
healthy patient demand and improved realization, led by a favorable payor mix shift. This was 
partially offset by relatively moderated growth across our Gujarat centers, largely on account of 
deliberate rationalization of institutional mix to improve profitability.  
Turning to the East cluster. Revenue stood at INR 928 million, representing 23% year-on-year 
growth and contributing 11% to our overall revenue. Growth was led by a 18% increase in 
patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 5% year-on-year. Growth was broad-based across 
the region, led by a strong performance at Ranchi. Our international Kenya operations, the 
revenue stood at INR 302 million, registering approximately 54% year-on-year growth during 
the quarter. 
 
Performance was supported by stronger patient inflows across radiation oncology, aided by the 
addition of a new radiation therapy machine, as well as increased medical oncology therapies 
following the addition of 13 new beds.  
I would also like to highlight some of the key developments during the quarter.  
During Q2 FY 2027, we added 25 operational beds across our network, comprising 13 beds in 
Kenya, seven beds in Kolkata, and five beds at Nagpur. With these additions, we have 
operationalized a total of 146 beds in H1 FY 2027, further strengthening our capacity across 
existing and newer facilities. 
 
Alongside capacity expansion, we continued to invest in advanced medical technologies. During 
the quarter, we operationalized the MR-LINAC, a highly advanced adaptive radiation therapy 
system at our North Bengaluru hospital, and added a cardiac surgical robotic system at our multi-
specialty hospital in Ahmedabad, further strengthening our technology-led treatment 
capabilities. 
 
On the clinical front, key milestones included the first CAR T-cell therapy at HCG Ahmedabad, 
the introduction of a robotic breast surgical system at KR Road, Bengaluru, robotic spine 
surgery at HCG Rajkot, and transoral robotic surgery at HCG Vadodara. We also launched a 
1,212-gene liquid biopsy panel and introduced two new nuclear medicine tracers at KR Hospital, 
Bengaluru, enhancing our precision diagnostics capabilities. Our clinical expertise is also 
reflected in several complex cases managed across our network. 
 
These included a limb-saving surgery in a 28-day-old infant, precision radiosurgery using 
CyberKnife to reduce a tumor encircling the optic nerve without any vision loss, and complex 
shoulder tumor reconstruction using customized 3D-printed titanium implants. These cases 
demonstrate our ability to combine multidisciplinary expertise with advanced technologies to 
manage complex cancers while prioritizing organ preservation and patient outcomes.  
 
Lastly, I would like to briefly address the recent regulatory developments concerning trade 
margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. 

Page 4 of 14 
 
 
We recognize the importance of making cancer treatment more affordable and accessible. This 
aligns with HCG's philosophy of treating cancer right the first time, which emphasizes 
delivering high-quality, comprehensive cancer care with the best possible clinical outcomes. 
The regulatory measures apply to a specific subset of oncology drugs, with implications varying 
depending on the drug portfolio, pricing arrangements, and payor mix. 
 
Based on our assessment on an absolute basis, we estimate a mid-to-high single-digit percentage 
impact to EBITDA on an annualized basis. While we anticipate some near-term impact as the 
regulatory framework takes effect, we remain confident in the strength of our underlying growth 
drivers. Rising cancer incidence, along with improved screening and affordability, is continuing 
to support sustained demand for high-quality cancer care. 
 
We remain focused on serving this opportunity through continued growth in patient volumes, 
improved asset utilization, revenue mix optimization, and identified operational improvement 
levers across our network. We believe these initiatives will support sustainable long-term 
growth and value creation for our stakeholders. With this, I would like to hand over the call to 
Sanjeev, who will briefly take us through our H1 FY 2027 financial performance, following 
which we will open the floor for questions.   
Sanjeev Kumar: 
Thank you, Manish. Good afternoon, everyone. Let me take you through our financial 
performance for the first half of FY 2027, along with an update on our balance sheet. We 
delivered healthy financial performance during the first half, supported by revenue growth, 
improving quality of revenue, and operating efficiencies.  
Consolidated revenue for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 14,100 million, representing growth of 15% 
year-on-year basis. This revenue growth was driven by a 9% increase in patient volume and 6% 
growth in ARPP. The improvement in ARPP was largely supported by a favorable payor mix 
and an increasing contribution from high-end procedures, including robotic surgeries.  
Adjusted EBITDA for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 2,740 million, registering a growth of 18% on 
year-on-year basis. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved by 84 basis points to 19.7% compared 
with 18.8% in H1 FY 2026, reflecting continued improvement in the quality of revenue and 
operating efficiencies. 
 
During the quarter, we also recognized an ESOP expense of INR 29.8 million arising from the 
grant of ESOPs in September 2026. Please note that this is a non-cash expense. Now moving to 
other financial items. Depreciation and amortization expenses for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 
1,365 million as compared with INR 1,176 million in the corresponding period last year, 
showing an increase of 16%, primarily reflecting investments in capacity expansion, including 
North Bengaluru. 
 
Finance costs declined by 11% year-on-year to INR 775 million as compared to INR 876 million 
in H1 FY 2026, supported by debt repayments of INR 1,700 million during the first half of this 
year. At the bottom line, adjusted PAT after normalizing the impact of extraordinary expense 
was INR 287 million in H1 2027, representing a growth of 30% year-on-year basis. Now turning 

Page 5 of 14 
 
to our balance sheet. 
 
Net debt excluding capital leases stood at INR 5,751 million as of September 30, 2026. During 
the first half, we also incurred a capex of INR 1,279 million, primarily towards capacity 
expansion, medical equipment, and infrastructure upgrades across our network. We remain 
disciplined in our approach to capital allocation, balancing investments in growth with prudent 
debt management and a continued focus on improving returns on capital. With that, we would 
be happy to open the floor for questions. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, sir. We will now begin with the question and answer session.   We have the first 
question from the line of Aditya Chheda from InCred Asset Management & Alternative 
Investments.   
Aditya Chheda: 
Hi, on the price cap exposure, could you walk us through the rough math on how we can arrive 
at this mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA impact? My second question is about the EPCG 
provision impact. I think the total contingent liability is about INR 75 crore. So how much of 
the further impact is left, and what is the cash flow impact from the same? 
Manish Mattoo: 
Thanks, Aditya. On the first one, we have to understand that these 137 drugs which came under 
the capping represent a small subset of the overall oncology portfolio, the medical oncology 
portfolio. That is point number one. While it will be difficult to get into very minute details on 
how we have arrived at impact, suffice to say that on an annualized basis, this is going to be 
mid-single digit to high single digit. 
 
More importantly, I think how we are thinking about this, there are several levers that we have 
at play so that we can address this in the near to medium term through the trade channel 
optimization. Patient volumes will expand. There is then going to be an improved asset 
utilization. Revenue optimization has continued to deliver for us the last couple of quarters, and 
that will continue to remain on track. 
 
Of course, several operating efficiencies that will be at play, which will help us be on track as 
to our earlier estimates that we have continued to give. I request Sanjeev to address the EPCG 
question. 
Sanjeev Kumar: 
Yes, hi. We recognize an exceptional expense of INR 116 million towards provisioning related 
to the EPCG. This follows a detailed assessment of all our export obligations, and we believe 
the necessary provisioning has been now adequately accounted for. Accordingly, we do not 
anticipate any further material provisions in the near term. I hope I have answered this question. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Got it. Was there an equal cash flow impact because of the same from Q1 and Q2? We had 
almost INR 16 crore. 
Sanjeev Kumar: 
At present, there is no cash impact as of now. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Okay. On the first question, Manish, which you answered, what I was seeking is that, say, 
whatever the 137 drugs were, where, let us say, 15% or 20% of revenue and the margins earlier 
would have been X, and now it would be, let us say, 30%. Any math around that, but if it is 

Page 6 of 14 
 
possible. Otherwise, we can discuss later. Thanks. 
Manish Mattoo: 
Yes, we can discuss that later, Aditya. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Okay, thank you. 
Moderator 
Thank you.   We have the next question from the line of Devang Patel from Sameeksha Capital.   
Devang Patel: 
My first question was on the new Bengaluru hospital  so, that had some negative impact on the 
margins this quarter. How long do you expect that drag to continue? 
Manish Mattoo: 
Devang, as we had communicated in Q1 also, the revenue ramp-up is happening as per the 
expectations. The revenue is obviously on a run rate basis improved from Q1 to Q2, and the 
losses are narrowing. In Q1, we had a loss of INR 7.5 crore for the quarter. In Q2, it has come

Sanjeev Kumar: 
Actually, we are referring to the monthly EBITDA breakeven. 
Moderator 
Thank you. We have the next question from the line of Sumit Gupta from Antique Stock Broking

Sumit Gupta: 
Hi, Manish. With respect to the growth part, I want to understand, as of now, the growth rate is

Manish Mattoo: 
Sumit, our guidance has been around mid-teens growth, coupled by high teens to 20% EBITDA

Sumit Gupta: 
Okay. With respect to Gujarat, basically the West cluster, we did write Gujarat is giving a sub-

Manish Mattoo: 
I think Gujarat should be back to the mid-teens growth by Q4 of this year. That is what we are

Sumit Gupta:

Manish Mattoo: 
Very difficult to quantify that impact. Overall, I think we are confident of delivering the mid-

that should help us get to where we are aiming to go. 
Sumit Gupta: 
Understood. Another question on the onco drugs.   
Sumit Gupta: 
Basically, of the overall onco drugs set that you utilize for the operations, so how many are

Manish Mattoo: 
I think majority of the drugs are under the trade margin cap now, barring, I think,

Thank you. 
Moderator

Gopal Bhatt: 
My first question is just regarding the, you guys mentioning the impact of these trade margin

Manish Mattoo:

Gopal Bhatt: 
Okay. Starting Q3, basically for, yes, so for November. You did not see any impact in October.

Manish Mattoo:

Gopal Bhatt: 
Okay. And if I would just actually step back a bit and ask you a broader question on the 
regulation as well. I mean, where do you see the Government's intentions with the I mean, 
actually, sorry, it is rather the Supreme Court-driven thing, but still, where do you see the 
broader regulatory landscape sort of shaping up, and what do you see, and I mean, an acceptable

Manish Mattoo: 
Gopal, I mean, it is evolving, right? As the needs of the country evolve, and so does this 
regulatory environment. While there is been a lot of investment in the healthcare space over the

So, I think this is evolving, and I think the right balance will be arrived at through negotiations, 
consultations, where the Government, which has been open to hearing our perspective too, and 
taking a balanced stand on that. I think we have seen that also happen. But the focus remains for 
us is on delivering high-quality care, and I think that itself will make sure that we deliver the

I think the inherent demand in the system and need for high-quality care in India will remain to

like to leave it.

Manish Mattoo:

Gopal Bhatt:

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited 
Earnings Conference Call.   Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the 
conference over to Mr. Anoop Poojari from CDR India.   
Anoop Poojari: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on HealthCare Global 
Enterprises Q2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings conference call. We have with us Dr. Manish Mattoo, 
Executive Director and CEO of the company, Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Chief Financial Officer, and 
Mr. Ravi Gothwal, Head of Investor Relations. We would like to begin the call with opening 
remarks from Manish, following which we will have the forum open for an interactive question-
and-answer session. 
 
Before we start, I would like to point out that some statements made in today's call may be 
forward-looking in nature, and a disclaimer to this effect has been included in the earnings 
presentation shared with you earlier. I would now like to invite Manish to make his opening 
remarks. 
Manish Mattoo: 
Thank you, Anoop. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us for HCG's Quarter 
2 and H1 FY27 earnings call.  
I am pleased to share that we have sustained our growth momentum into the second quarter, 
supported by healthy patient demand and improving revenue mix, and steady progress across 
our strategic and operational priorities. As highlighted in our previous earnings call, our strategic 
priorities remain centered on profitable growth, improving asset utilization, strengthening 
clinical differentiation, and optimizing our revenue mix. 
 
We are encouraged by the progress made during the quarter across all these areas. Coming to 
our financial performance, I would like to highlight that all financial figures presented today 
exclude the Milann Fertility business, which was divested in June 2026. The corresponding 
prior-year figures have also been adjusted accordingly to ensure a like-for-like comparison. 
 
In Quarter 2 FY 2027, HCG delivered revenue of INR 7,318 million, representing a growth of 
16% year- on- year. Revenue growth, excluding our North Bengaluru new hospital, was 14% 

Page 2 of 14 
 
year- on- year. The growth was broad-based across our operating clusters, primarily driven by 
a 9% increase in patient volumes, while average revenue per patient increased by 7% year-on- 
year. 
 
The improvement in ARPP was supported by a favorable payor mix and an increasing 
contribution from high-complexity oncology treatments. This included a 37% year-on-year 
increase in robotic surgeries, alongside growing adoption of other advanced therapies and 
surgical procedures across our network. 
 
As we have consistently emphasized, our objective is not merely to drive higher patient 
volumes, but to enhance the quantity and quality of our revenues through a greater contribution 
from complex oncology procedures and improved payor mix, superior clinical outcomes, and 
higher productivity across our specialized oncology ecosystem. 
 
In line with this strategy, we continue to focus on expanding our non-institutional business while 
progressively optimizing our exposure to lower-realization segments. These efforts are yielding 
encouraging results, with non-institutional revenue growing by 21% year-on-year, resulting in 
an improvement of over 300 basis points in its revenue share to 69%.  
On the profitability front, EBITDA for the quarter, including North Bengaluru loss of INR 61 
million, was INR 1,425 million, representing growth of 17% year-on-year, with EBITDA 
margins improved to 19.7% compared to 19.2% in Q2FY26. 
 
While we continue to benefit from improving revenue quality and operating efficiencies, margin 
expansion during the quarter was partly moderated due to incremental employee cost amounting 
to approximately INR 60 million on account of revision in Karnataka Wage Act 2026. 
 
If you really look at it on a like-to-like basis, excluding the wage revision impact, EBITDA 
growth was over 20% year-on-year. North Bengaluru, our newest hospital, continued to make 
good progress, with its EBITDA loss reducing to INR 61 million during this quarter. Our focus 
remains on accelerating clinical ramp-up, improving capacity utilization, and progressively 
reducing operating losses. 
 
Let me now take you through the performance across our operating clusters.  
Starting with the South cluster, the revenue stood at INR 2,941 million. Delivering a strong 
growth of 18% and contributing to 40% of our overall revenue. Growth was supported by a 14% 
improvement in ARPP and a 4% increase in patient volumes, with a strong contribution from 
our Bengaluru Center of Excellence and the progressive ramp-up of our North Bengaluru 
hospital. 
 
ARPP improvement across the cluster was also aided by a favorable payor mix and higher 
contribution of high-end procedures and therapies.  
Moving to the West cluster. Revenue stood at INR 3,147 million, registering 10% year-on-year 
growth and contributing 43% to overall revenue. Growth was primarily driven by a 7% increase 
in patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 3%, supported by a favorable payor mix. 

Page 3 of 14 
 
 
The Maharashtra region delivered a strong performance with a mid-teens growth, driven by 
healthy patient demand and improved realization, led by a favorable payor mix shift. This was 
partially offset by relatively moderated growth across our Gujarat centers, largely on account of 
deliberate rationalization of institutional mix to improve profitability.  
Turning to the East cluster. Revenue stood at INR 928 million, representing 23% year-on-year 
growth and contributing 11% to our overall revenue. Growth was led by a 18% increase in 
patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 5% year-on-year. Growth was broad-based across 
the region, led by a strong performance at Ranchi. Our international Kenya operations, the 
revenue stood at INR 302 million, registering approximately 54% year-on-year growth during 
the quarter. 
 
Performance was supported by stronger patient inflows across radiation oncology, aided by the 
addition of a new radiation therapy machine, as well as increased medical oncology therapies 
following the addition of 13 new beds.  
I would also like to highlight some of the key developments during the quarter.  
During Q2 FY 2027, we added 25 operational beds across our network, comprising 13 beds in 
Kenya, seven beds in Kolkata, and five beds at Nagpur. With these additions, we have 
operationalized a total of 146 beds in H1 FY 2027, further strengthening our capacity across 
existing and newer facilities. 
 
Alongside capacity expansion, we continued to invest in advanced medical technologies. During 
the quarter, we operationalized the MR-LINAC, a highly advanced adaptive radiation therapy 
system at our North Bengaluru hospital, and added a cardiac surgical robotic system at our multi-
specialty hospital in Ahmedabad, further strengthening our technology-led treatment 
capabilities. 
 
On the clinical front, key milestones included the first CAR T-cell therapy at HCG Ahmedabad, 
the introduction of a robotic breast surgical system at KR Road, Bengaluru, robotic spine 
surgery at HCG Rajkot, and transoral robotic surgery at HCG Vadodara. We also launched a 
1,212-gene liquid biopsy panel and introduced two new nuclear medicine tracers at KR Hospital, 
Bengaluru, enhancing our precision diagnostics capabilities. Our clinical expertise is also 
reflected in several complex cases managed across our network. 
 
These included a limb-saving surgery in a 28-day-old infant, precision radiosurgery using 
CyberKnife to reduce a tumor encircling the optic nerve without any vision loss, and complex 
shoulder tumor reconstruction using customized 3D-printed titanium implants. These cases 
demonstrate our ability to combine multidisciplinary expertise with advanced technologies to 
manage complex cancers while prioritizing organ preservation and patient outcomes.  
 
Lastly, I would like to briefly address the recent regulatory developments concerning trade 
margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. 

Page 4 of 14 
 
 
We recognize the importance of making cancer treatment more affordable and accessible. This 
aligns with HCG's philosophy of treating cancer right the first time, which emphasizes 
delivering high-quality, comprehensive cancer care with the best possible clinical outcomes. 
The regulatory measures apply to a specific subset of oncology drugs, with implications varying 
depending on the drug portfolio, pricing arrangements, and payor mix. 
 
Based on our assessment on an absolute basis, we estimate a mid-to-high single-digit percentage 
impact to EBITDA on an annualized basis. While we anticipate some near-term impact as the 
regulatory framework takes effect, we remain confident in the strength of our underlying growth 
drivers. Rising cancer incidence, along with improved screening and affordability, is continuing 
to support sustained demand for high-quality cancer care. 
 
We remain focused on serving this opportunity through continued growth in patient volumes, 
improved asset utilization, revenue mix optimization, and identified operational improvement 
levers across our network. We believe these initiatives will support sustainable long-term 
growth and value creation for our stakeholders. With this, I would like to hand over the call to 
Sanjeev, who will briefly take us through our H1 FY 2027 financial performance, following 
which we will open the floor for questions.   
Sanjeev Kumar: 
Thank you, Manish. Good afternoon, everyone. Let me take you through our financial 
performance for the first half of FY 2027, along with an update on our balance sheet. We 
delivered healthy financial performance during the first half, supported by revenue growth, 
improving quality of revenue, and operating efficiencies.  
Consolidated revenue for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 14,100 million, representing growth of 15% 
year-on-year basis. This revenue growth was driven by a 9% increase in patient volume and 6% 
growth in ARPP. The improvement in ARPP was largely supported by a favorable payor mix 
and an increasing contribution from high-end procedures, including robotic surgeries.  
Adjusted EBITDA for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 2,740 million, registering a growth of 18% on 
year-on-year basis. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved by 84 basis points to 19.7% compared 
with 18.8% in H1 FY 2026, reflecting continued improvement in the quality of revenue and 
operating efficiencies. 
 
During the quarter, we also recognized an ESOP expense of INR 29.8 million arising from the 
grant of ESOPs in September 2026. Please note that this is a non-cash expense. Now moving to 
other financial items. Depreciation and amortization expenses for H1 FY 2027 stood at INR 
1,365 million as compared with INR 1,176 million in the corresponding period last year, 
showing an increase of 16%, primarily reflecting investments in capacity expansion, including 
North Bengaluru. 
 
Finance costs declined by 11% year-on-year to INR 775 million as compared to INR 876 million 
in H1 FY 2026, supported by debt repayments of INR 1,700 million during the first half of this 
year. At the bottom line, adjusted PAT after normalizing the impact of extraordinary expense 
was INR 287 million in H1 2027, representing a growth of 30% year-on-year basis. Now turning 

Page 5 of 14 
 
to our balance sheet. 
 
Net debt excluding capital leases stood at INR 5,751 million as of September 30, 2026. During 
the first half, we also incurred a capex of INR 1,279 million, primarily towards capacity 
expansion, medical equipment, and infrastructure upgrades across our network. We remain 
disciplined in our approach to capital allocation, balancing investments in growth with prudent 
debt management and a continued focus on improving returns on capital. With that, we would 
be happy to open the floor for questions. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, sir. We will now begin with the question and answer session.   We have the first 
question from the line of Aditya Chheda from InCred Asset Management & Alternative 
Investments.   
Aditya Chheda: 
Hi, on the price cap exposure, could you walk us through the rough math on how we can arrive 
at this mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA impact? My second question is about the EPCG 
provision impact. I think the total contingent liability is about INR 75 crore. So how much of 
the further impact is left, and what is the cash flow impact from the same? 
Manish Mattoo: 
Thanks, Aditya. On the first one, we have to understand that these 137 drugs which came under 
the capping represent a small subset of the overall oncology portfolio, the medical oncology 
portfolio. That is point number one. While it will be difficult to get into very minute details on 
how we have arrived at impact, suffice to say that on an annualized basis, this is going to be 
mid-single digit to high single digit. 
 
More importantly, I think how we are thinking about this, there are several levers that we have 
at play so that we can address this in the near to medium term through the trade channel 
optimization. Patient volumes will expand. There is then going to be an improved asset 
utilization. Revenue optimization has continued to deliver for us the last couple of quarters, and 
that will continue to remain on track. 
 
Of course, several operating efficiencies that will be at play, which will help us be on track as 
to our earlier estimates that we have continued to give. I request Sanjeev to address the EPCG 
question. 
Sanjeev Kumar: 
Yes, hi. We recognize an exceptional expense of INR 116 million towards provisioning related 
to the EPCG. This follows a detailed assessment of all our export obligations, and we believe 
the necessary provisioning has been now adequately accounted for. Accordingly, we do not 
anticipate any further material provisions in the near term. I hope I have answered this question. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Got it. Was there an equal cash flow impact because of the same from Q1 and Q2? We had 
almost INR 16 crore. 
Sanjeev Kumar: 
At present, there is no cash impact as of now. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Okay. On the first question, Manish, which you answered, what I was seeking is that, say, 
whatever the 137 drugs were, where, let us say, 15% or 20% of revenue and the margins earlier 
would have been X, and now it would be, let us say, 30%. Any math around that, but if it is 

Page 6 of 14 
 
possible. Otherwise, we can discuss later. Thanks. 
Manish Mattoo: 
Yes, we can discuss that later, Aditya. 
Aditya Chheda: 
Okay, thank you. 
Moderator 
Thank you.   We have the next question from the line of Devang Patel from Sameeksha Capital.   
Devang Patel: 
My first question was on the new Bengaluru hospital  so, that had some negative impact on the 
margins this quarter. How long do you expect that drag to continue? 
Manish Mattoo: 
Devang, as we had communicated in Q1 also, the revenue ramp-up is happening as per the 
expectations. The revenue is obviously on a run rate basis improved from Q1 to Q2, and the 
losses are narrowing. In Q1, we had a loss of INR 7.5 crore for the quarter. In Q2, it has come 
down to about INR 6 crore. As stated earlier also, we are on track to hit monthly EBITDA 
breakeven by end of Q4 of this financial year. There is no change there. 
Sanjeev Kumar: 
Actually, we are referring to the monthly EBITDA breakeven. 
Moderator 
Thank you. We have the next question from the line of Sumit Gupta from Antique Stock Broking 
Limited.   
  
Sumit Gupta: 
Hi, Manish. With respect to the growth part, I want to understand, as of now, the growth rate is 
around 16%. When can we expect it to reach around 18% level?   
Manish Mattoo: 
Sumit, our guidance has been around mid-teens growth, coupled by high teens to 20% EBITDA 
growth, and we continue to stay on track as far as that is concerned. Of course, if there is any 
inorganic opportunity over and above this is all, of course, organic growth. Anything over and 
above this will add to that growth. But as of now, the guidance remains the same. 
Sumit Gupta: 
Okay. With respect to Gujarat, basically the West cluster, we did write Gujarat is giving a sub-
performance. By when can Gujarat be normalized, and we can expect it to grow in the future?

MANAGEMENT: MR. RAHUL GAUTAM – CHAIRMAN AND MANAGING

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Sheela Foam Limited Q2 H1 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Emkay Global Financial Services Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note 
that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Devanshu Bansal 
from Emkay Global Financial Services Limited. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Bansal. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Yes. Hi, good afternoon, everyone. I would like to welcome the management and thank them 
for this opportunity. We have with us today Rahul Gautam, Chairman and Managing Director; 
Tushaar Gautam, Vice Chairman and Joint Managing Director; Rakesh Chahar, Deputy 
Managing Director and Amit Kumar Gupta, Group Chief Financial Officer. I shall now hand 
over the call to the management for the opening remarks. Over to you, gentlemen. 
Rahul Gautam: 
Thank you, Devanshu. I just want to make a little correction that Tushaar Gautam is not available 
at this time. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining us to share our 
results for the second quarter Q2 and the first half, that is H1 of this year. I hope you've had the 
chance to go through the numbers and the presentations.  
Let me begin with the environment first. As it has already really shaped this quarter. From 
February onwards, this has been an absolutely unprecedented kind of time for our industry. On 
a ballpark, the crude is up by about 50%, and our 2 key raw materials have moved even more. 
Since mid-February, polyol, our main chemical or main raw material is up by 65% and TDI by 
33%. Sustained increases of this kind have simply not been seen before. 
 
The war has disrupted the entire supply chain and logistics. Some of the facilities in the Middle 
East have been partially destroyed and others are restricted because of the Hormuz blockage. 
Additionally, the festive season, which was in late September last year, moved into October this 
time, resulting in a shift of demand from Q2 to Q3.
