Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Sheela Foam Limited Q2 H1 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Emkay Global Financial Services Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note 
that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Devanshu Bansal 
from Emkay Global Financial Services Limited. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Bansal. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Yes. Hi, good afternoon, everyone. I would like to welcome the management and thank them 
for this opportunity. We have with us today Rahul Gautam, Chairman and Managing Director; 
Tushaar Gautam, Vice Chairman and Joint Managing Director; Rakesh Chahar, Deputy 
Managing Director and Amit Kumar Gupta, Group Chief Financial Officer. I shall now hand 
over the call to the management for the opening remarks. Over to you, gentlemen. 
Rahul Gautam: 
Thank you, Devanshu. I just want to make a little correction that Tushaar Gautam is not available 
at this time. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining us to share our 
results for the second quarter Q2 and the first half, that is H1 of this year. I hope you've had the 
chance to go through the numbers and the presentations.  
Let me begin with the environment first. As it has already really shaped this quarter. From 
February onwards, this has been an absolutely unprecedented kind of time for our industry. On 
a ballpark, the crude is up by about 50%, and our 2 key raw materials have moved even more. 
Since mid-February, polyol, our main chemical or main raw material is up by 65% and TDI by 
33%. Sustained increases of this kind have simply not been seen before. 
 
The war has disrupted the entire supply chain and logistics. Some of the facilities in the Middle 
East have been partially destroyed and others are restricted because of the Hormuz blockage. 
Additionally, the festive season, which was in late September last year, moved into October this 
time, resulting in a shift of demand from Q2 to Q3.  
However, we recognize that these are the times, where the strength of a leader shows. Our first 
responsibility when things get this hard is to keep serving our customers, and that is what we 
did. We kept material flowing through supplier relationships that have been built over decades 
at a time when many of the smaller unorganized players simply could not source or hold their 
prices.  
With the strength of the brands, we've had the advantage of being able to pass these increases 
on to the market and eventually to the consumer. The consumer has his own affordability 
benchmarks also. A customer who comes in with about INR20,000 to spend on a mattress can 
stretch a bit, but not to the full impact of the large price increase.  
The same money now buys him a slightly lower category of the product, and that change impacts 
us even when values may hold up. With demand still soft, we have chosen to spend more and 

 
 
Sheela Foam Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026

not less on our brands, advertising and consumer schemes. We went out and launched the Great 
Sleepwell Festival across the country.  
It has turned out one of the strongest schemes we have ever introduced for our consumers. This 
does take off some profitability in the near term, but it has built a healthy pipeline of demand, 
as we go into the festive quarters of the second half. The outcome is that even after a margin hit, 
we have held our profitability in absolute terms. 
 
In a quarter like this, protecting the core of the business while still investing in it was important 
to us. The numbers tell the story quite clearly. On a consolidated basis, revenue for the quarter 
grew by about 19% to a level of INR1,045 crores. The first time that we have crossed the 
INR1,000 crores revenue number in Q2 and also our third consecutive quarter of a 15% plus 
growth.  
Our operating EBITDA for the quarter was INR87 crores, almost the same as we delivered in 
the corresponding quarter a year ago. PAT was INR46 crores, and that is about 5x of last year. 
Coming to the half year, revenue grew about 22% to a level of INR2,076 crores -- INR2,077 
crores, and the operating EBITDA grew 23% to a INR200 crores mark from INR162 crores last 
year at a margin of 9.6%.  
And I must also add that the PAT rose to INR109 crores, that is more than 6x last year. Though 
we clocked higher gross margins than the first quarter of this year, our investment in brand and 
marketing kept our operating EBITDA margins neutral. I now want to spend a little time on 
Furlenco because I believe it genuinely changes the picture of our group. 
 
From 1st October, this year, Furlenco has become a subsidiary of Sheela Foam. This is not a 
sudden step. It is something we have worked towards for some time and widen our reach, our 
scale and the very nature of what we do. Let me explain the business because it is very different 
from our existing business. Furlenco is primarily a furniture rental company. 
 
It gives people in our cities access to well-designed furniture and that too on a subscription basis 
without having to own anything or everything. We think nobody would want to rent these things. 
That is what we have always been thinking. But today, it is not only the floating population, it 
is people who simply like a change, who want their furniture kept in good shape, who move 
homes or move cities are indulging in this offer.  
Furlenco offers them a catalog of more than 300 products. It is present in more than 30 cities. It 
has a subscriber base of more than 200,000 or 2 lakh subscribers, and it runs a disciplined asset-
based model, keeping the asset utilization much above 90%. That discipline is what makes it 
profitable.  
What this business has done in a short time says a great deal about our ability to spot value and 
build it. When we invested in FY '24, Furlenco had a revenue of about INR139 crores and had 
a subscriber base of 70,000. It was also losing close to INR130 crores a year. Post the turnaround, 
this year, we expect it to close at INR500 crores mark with an EBITDA margin of about 40% 
from deep losses to a profitable business with revenue almost 4x where it was in about 3 years 
and still growing at more than 30%.  

 
 
Sheela Foam Limited

That is Furlenco today. The recent trend is the same in the first half for Furlenco. The revenue 
has grown about 34% -- and to 34% to INR229 crores, and EBITDA was also up by about 69% 
to a level of INR89 crores. An attractive subscriber base has grown 35% over the previous year.  
This is a space whose time has come. Furniture rental is finding real acceptance and particularly 
with the younger and Gen Z consumers, who value flexibility far more than ownership. The 
capital markets have taken a note as well with one of the players in this space having listed 
recently. All of this changes what Sheela Foam as a group is today. 
 
We have enhanced our B2C portfolio in many growth areas, a house of more than 13 brands 
held together by one idea that has guided us from the very beginning, the science of comfort for 
all the consumers that we deal with. The group today stands on primarily 4 pillars. First is 
mattress, where we serve every kind of a customer from mass to premium to luxury.  
Sleepwell and Kurlon sit at the premium and economy end. Tarang and Aram give us depth and 
reach across the value segments and Chattam & Wells and Nature's Rest take us into luxury. The 
second pillar is furniture in both rental and retail, led by Furlenco and alongside with our entry 
into branded furniture retail also under the flagship brands of Sleepwell and Kurlon.  
The third category or the third pillar is foam and cushioning. Our technical and industrial foam 
business under B2B category as well as B2C with brands such as FeatherFoam and Jumpz HR 
etcetera, work well in this area. This caters not only to consumers, but to a much wider set of 
industries with applications ranging from automotive to footwear and our foam has long been a 
benchmark across all of them.  
And the fourth is the international subsidiaries and the IT initiative that we have. Our business 
abroad, Joyce in Australia and Interplasp in Spain and our enterprise technology and digital 
solutions company, Staqo, have all been doing extremely well. Sheela Foam today is a broad-
based consumer company with brands at home and abroad across categories, channels, price 
points and markets.  
As these pieces come together, we expect the combined group to close this year at a revenue of 
around INR5,000 crores with an EBITDA of roughly INR600 crores, a margin a little above 
12%. I must also add that the international businesses remain strong and profitable. In Spain, the 
revenue grew well. 
 
We took on new customers during the quarter and their volumes will begin to show from the 
second half. The cost of winning and servicing did weigh on Spain's margin this quarter, but 
that, to my mind, is money well spent for the growth ahead. For the half, Spain has already 
delivered an EBITDA margin of over 10%, actually 10.7%.  
In Australia, Joyce can well -- did well and ran well at the operating level with an EBITDA 
margin of also 10.7% in the quarter and 13.4% for the half year. The reported profit for the 
quarter has pulled down by a one-off provision we had to take against one of our key customers'

Beard going into administration. We expect to normalize this very soon. Our newer growth 
engines also continue to do well. On the D2C and e-commerce side, we are strong and continue 
to grow at a healthy pace, led by our own website, brand.com. The U2O business, which is the 
unorganized to organized business, which takes us from the unorganized to the organized market 
and has now reached more than 10,000 touch points or dealers and has grown by about 41%. 
 
And Staqo, as I mentioned, our technology company, keeps growing well, while holding a 
healthy EBITDA margins of around 28%. Let me close here. This was a quarter that tested us 
on every front, and I believe we managed to handle it reasonably well by standing with our 
customers, investing through the cycle and holding the profitability of the business to the 
previous levels.  
With Furlenco now part of the family, the portfolio is wide, is actually very bright. I'm confident 
that Sheela Foam will continue its growth trajectory going forward. With that, I will ask our 
Group CFO, Mr. Amit Kumar Gupta, to take us through the financials in more detail. Thank you 
very much. 
Amit Kumar Gupta: 
Thank you, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, now let me take you through the financials for the quarter 
and the first half of the current financial year. On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations 
grew to INR1,045 crores, a growth of 19% over similar quarter last year, helped by both growth 
in mattresses as well as foam and a very strong growth in Australia and Spain.  
Operating EBITDA for the quarter was INR87 crores at a margin of 8.4%, broadly flat against 
INR87 crores a year ago. Reported EBITDA was INR83 crores. As Rahul sir explained, the 
pressure came from the sharp rise in polyol and TDI prices and the higher expense behind the 
Great Sleepwell festival. PAT for the quarter was INR46 crores against INR10 crores last year, 
close to 5x, helped by both operations and by lower finance cost and depreciation.  
Cash EPS for the quarter was INR8.3. For the half year, consolidated revenue grew by 22% to 
INR2,077 crores from INR1,696 crores. Operating EBITDA grew by about 23% to INR200 
crores from INR162 crores at a margin of 9.6%. The operating leverage of the first quarter was 
partly offset by raw material inflation in the second -- sorry, PAT for the second half rose to -- 
PAT for the first half rose to INR109 crores from INR17 crores last year for the similar period. 
And EPS grew to INR18.7 from a diluted EPS of around INR9.8 last year. On a stand-alone 
basis, revenue for the quarter grew 17% to INR781 crores with EBITDA at INR61 crores at a 
margin of 7.8%. For H1 this year stand-alone revenue grew by 18% to INR1,452 crores and 
EBITDA grew 5% to INR129 crores.  
At the segment level, for the first half, Mattress grew by 11% and Foam grew by 26%, with 
volumes broadly flat, reflecting the pricing actions and the festive season shift. On the business 
abroad, Australia and Joyce had half year revenue of -- in Australia, Joyce had a half year 
revenue of INR241 crores, a growth of 16% year-on-year and an operating EBITDA margin of 
around 13.4%. 
 
In Spain, Interplasp had half year revenue of INR250 crores at a growth of 44% and EBITDA 
margin of 10.7%. Furlenco, which became our subsidiary from 1st October, had a revenue of

I request the moderator to open the floor for questions. Thank you.

margins, but that will have a hit on the overall volumes that will be there.

Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Avinash Karumanchi from Motilal Oswal Financial 
Services Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Avinash Karumanchi: 
Good evening, everyone. On behalf of Motilal Oswal Financial Services, I welcome you to the 
Q2 
 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call of GNG Electronics Limited. Joining us on the call today 
are Mr. Sharad Khandelwal, Founder and Managing Director; Mr. Ajay Pancholi, Director; Mr. 
Raakesh Jhunjhunwala, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Rohit Aggarwal, Strategy and IR. 
 
Now I hand over the call to Sharadji for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Sharad Khandelwal: 
Good evening, and thank you, everyone. I welcome you all to the Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings call 
of GNG Electronics Limited. I'm very happy to share that we have delivered our best ever 
quarter. Revenue grew 42% year-on-year. This is our strongest quarterly growth since we listed, 
and this also makes it our best first half ever. 
 
What I find most encouraging is the quality of this growth. It was broad-based across India and 
our international market, across customer segments and across the channel. And it came with 
margin because customers are increasingly paying for what Electronics Bazaar stands for, a 
product that works like new, a warranty they can rely on and a partner they can trust. 
 
Rather than treating refurbished as a commodity, our laptops are sold as Electronics Bazaar 
refurbished laptops, which is a distinct brand positioning, and we are decommoditizing the 
refurbished space. 
 
We are solving the trust issue and trust is a huge margin lever. That is the shift we have been 
working towards and I believe it is what you are seeing in these numbers. Let me first take you 
through the quarter's performance, then the industry developments and then the progress across 
the company.  
For the quarter ended September 2026, our consolidated revenue stood at INR624.8 crores, 
which is up from INR439.9 crores in the same quarter last year. Gross margin improved by 515 
basis points year-on-year to 25.1%. Our India business grew 45% year-on-year and our  
international business grew by around 40%. Similarly, for the first half of FY27, revenue stood 
at INR1,037 crores, which is 38% up from the same period last year with gross margin expansion 
at 24.9%, which is an improvement of 438 basis points. Demand remains healthy across India 

 
 
GNG Electronics Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 17 
 
and our international markets, the United States, Europe and the Middle East, and we are ahead 
of our full year FY27 guidance on both revenue growth and profitability. 
 
Let me now spend a few minutes on the industry. On our last earnings call on 30th July, I had 
shared IDC's projection of a decline of around 20% in global PC shipments in the second half 
of calendar year 2026. IDC has since released its numbers for the September quarter, and the 
decline has come in at 20.1% year-on-year, which is 62.7 million units shipped as against 78.5 
million shipped in the same quarter last year. That's close to 16 million fewer computers in a 
single quarter. 
 
IDC attributes this to higher prices, supply constraints and inventory challenges and expects a 
decline of similar order in December quarter as well and prices are expected to remain elevated. 
For the full year 2026, IDC continues to project a decline of 11.3%, which is on a base of 284 
million computers sold in 2025 that's roughly 30 million decline of computers sold over last year 
and we are not factoring in any growth in computing demand. This is a very sharp decline for 
this industry and it is coming totally in the second half, that's from July to December of 2026. 
 
Now how long does this last? I would rather you hear it from the people who make the 
components and people who make the computers than from me.  
Michael Dell, the founder of Dell Technologies, said in an interview with CNBC on 13th 
October that he expects the memory shortage to get worse next year in terms of demand and 
supply. And that in his own words, it may well be a 4-year problem because there's just not 
enough supply.  
Sanjay Mehrotra, the Chief Executive of Micron, one of the 3 largest memory manufacturers in 
the world, said on its earnings call on 30th September 2026 that Micron expects memory and 
storage supply conditions to be and I quote "much tighter in fiscal year 2027 and 2028 than they 
were in 2026" and it does not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to 
balance.  
SK Hynix, the world's second largest memory manufacturer, reported in its results on 28th of 
October 2026, that's just a few days ago, that DRAM prices rose by a high-twenties percentage 
in a single quarter and NAND by mid-20s percentage. This is the second consecutive quarter of 
increase of that order. The Chief Financial Officer, Kim Woo-hyun, said and I quote "Memory 
supply cannot keep pace with this level of demand and growth" and described the shortfall as a 
constraint projected to continue through 2030. Its Chief Executive, Kwak Noh-jung, said the 
company's DRAM and HBM volumes for the next 3 years through 2029 are effectively sold out. 
 
The simple reading is that the large part of the world's memory capacity is going to AI and the 
personal computer is further back in the queue. This is now fully visible in the price of a new 
computer. A year ago, the sweet spot for a laptop in India was around INR35,000 to INR40,000. 
That same computer today is now between INR65,000 to INR72,000. And here is what that 
means for our customer. 
 
If a new computer costed INR100 earlier, our refurbished premium computer used to cost around 
INR30. We used to peg it at around 30% of a brand-new computer. The gap was INR 70. That 

 
 
GNG Electronics Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 17 
 
same new computer today costs INR180, which is an 80% increase from last year and ours has 
potential to go to INR54. 
 
If it goes to INR54, the gap will be around INR126. In absolute terms, the saving for the customer 
has almost doubled. And that's what has made the refurbished proposition even stronger. This 
will also allow us to peg our product as a percentage of a brand-new computer much above 30% 
than what we are currently doing. In case of phone or car market, the refurbished phone or car 
are typically sold at 45% to 50% price of a new car or a new phone. So this is a huge opportunity 
for us.  
What does this do to customer behavior? When the cost of a new technology rises, the 
conversation naturally shifts from ownership to access, value and usability. For a business, a 
college or a student, they still need a computer. The need has not gone anywhere, but they are 
now asking a different set of questions. Does every requirement need a brand-new device? Can 
the useful life of a good device be extended? How do I get reliable computing without putting 
more pressure on my budget? 
 
This is where we believe professionally refurbished devices have an increasingly important role 
to play, and it is what Electronics Bazaar has been built to offer, a premium refurbished device 
that works like new, looks like new and comes with a credible warranty of one to three years at 
a fraction of the price of new. 
 
The story for Electronics Bazaar refurbished computer is only starting.  
Having said all that, I want to be very clear on one point because I know that it's on your mind. 
Every time a new computer gets more expensive, the case for Electronics Bazaar gets stronger. 
But our case was strong before and it will be strong after. Elevated memory prices are a near-
term catalyst for us. They are not the foundation of our business. Our long-term growth is not 
dependent on the memory price cycle, and we believe the refurbished PC market will continue 
to expand even if memory prices moderate because what is driving it is a structural shift towards 
affordability, reliability and sustainability. 
 
Let me explain why we say that. On affordability, even before the shortage, we price a premium 
refurbished device at around 30% of the price of new. That gap does not close when memory 
prices moderate. And should memory prices correct someday, never say never, we have a big 
cushion. Our significant inventory is sourced at old prices. And because the absolute saving for 
the customer is now far greater, we can peg our product at a higher share of the new prices than 
before. In cars and phone, as I just said, pre-owned sells at 40% to 50% of new. We are at 30%.  
On reliability, the hesitation that once surrounded refurbished has reduced because of product 
quality, a 1- to 3-year warranty and a buying experience customers can rely on. That is trust built 
over time.  
On sustainability, enterprises and governments are increasingly asked to extend the life of what 
they own and to reduce e-waste and a professionally refurbished device answers both. 

 
 
GNG Electronics Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 17 
 
 
And underneath all of this is the headroom that existed before any of this began. 1 billion people 
in India carry a phone, 60 million own a computer. We know which number we are working on. 
We have 30 crore students in this country and only a small fraction of them have access to a 
computer.  
 
And we are a scaled operator in this market with deep sourcing relationships, in-house 
refurbishment capability and a strong global distribution network. 
 
These 3 reinforce each other, and that's what makes this a very, very compounding business. 
 
Let me now turn to what we have done this quarter. First, on the reach. Through our distribution 
network, our national distributors, our regional and city distributors and our channel partners, 
Electronics Bazaar products are today available across the length and breadth of India from 
metros to Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and towns and the pin codes, which continue to grow month-
over-month.

Nagpur, Indore, Rajkot, Amritsar, Madurai, Prayagraj, Asansol and Pimpri-Chinchwad. 
Alongside these, our team sat down with channel partners for Chai Pe Charcha sessions in over 
70 towns across 17 states and union territories from Dibrugarh in Assam to Tuticorin in Tamil 
Nadu, from Amritsar to Kolkata. And most of these were Tier 3 towns, places like Jhansi, 
Sivakasi, Kishangarh, the Lakhimpur Kheri, Gadchiroli and Wayanad. That is what reach means 
in practice, sitting with the partners in his own town over a cup of tea. The EB Elite program 
that we launched in Q1 now has 152 partners enrolled. We also opened our first exclusive 
Electronics Bazaar stores for small and medium businesses in Jaipur in partnership with our 
channel partner, Techjack. It's a dedicated space where an SMB customer can see the product, 
understand the warranty and buy with confidence and it gives us a template we can replicate in 
other cities. 
 
I also spent time on the ground myself this quarter in Jaipur, Chennai and Kolkata and in New 
York, Dallas, Los Angeles and Paris. And I make it a point to speak to at least 3 dealers or 
customers every single day wherever I am. What I hear is consistent, the product is accepted, 
the warranty is valued and the demand is there. Increasingly, customers walk into dealers and 
ask for Electronics Bazaar by name. Our job is to keep reaching them. 
 
Internationally, we participated in 2 of the most important industry gatherings of the year. In 
August, we were at ITAD Summit in Las Vegas, the principal conference for the IT Asset 
Disposition industry in the United States where the buyers and sellers of the corporate IT assets 
meet. And in October, we participated in the European Broker Meet in Vilamoura, Portugal, one 
of the largest annual gatherings of IT hardware brokers, refurbishers and distributors in Europe. 
The response we received at both was excellent. Across the 2 events, our team held more than 
250 meetings with sourcing and distribution partners. Both events reinforced the acceptance of 
Electronics Bazaar as a credible global partner on the sourcing side as much as on the selling 
side. 

 
 
GNG Electronics Limited 
 
 
November 03, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 17

Sharad Khandelwal: 
Good evening, and thank you, everyone. I welcome you all to the Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings call 
of GNG Electronics Limited. I'm very happy to share that we have delivered our best ever 
quarter. Revenue grew 42% year-on-year. This is our strongest quarterly growth since we listed, 
and this also makes it our best first half ever. 
 
What I find most encouraging is the quality of this growth. It was broad-based across India and 
our international market, across customer segments and across the channel. And it came with 
margin because customers are increasingly paying for what Electronics Bazaar stands for, a 
product that works like new, a warranty they can rely on and a partner they can trust. 
 
Rather than treating refurbished as a commodity, our laptops are sold as Electronics Bazaar 
refurbished laptops, which is a distinct brand positioning, and we are decommoditizing the 
refurbished space. 
 
We are solving the trust issue and trust is a huge margin lever. That is the shift we have been 
working towards and I believe it is what you are seeing in these numbers. Let me first take you 
through the quarter's performance, then the industry developments and then the progress across 
the company.  
For the quarter ended September 2026, our consolidated revenue stood at INR624.8 crores, 
which is up from INR439.9 crores in the same quarter last year. Gross margin improved by 515 
basis points year-on-year to 25.1%. Our India business grew 45% year-on-year and our  
international business grew by around 40%. Similarly, for the first half of FY27, revenue stood 
at INR1,037 crores, which is 38% up from the same period last year with gross margin expansion 
at 24.9%, which is an improvement of 438 basis points. Demand remains healthy across India

November 03, 2026

and our international markets, the United States, Europe and the Middle East, and we are ahead 
of our full year FY27 guidance on both revenue growth and profitability. 
 
Let me now spend a few minutes on the industry. On our last earnings call on 30th July, I had 
shared IDC's projection of a decline of around 20% in global PC shipments in the second half 
of calendar year 2026. IDC has since released its numbers for the September quarter, and the 
decline has come in at 20.1% year-on-year, which is 62.7 million units shipped as against 78.5 
million shipped in the same quarter last year. That's close to 16 million fewer computers in a 
single quarter. 
 
IDC attributes this to higher prices, supply constraints and inventory challenges and expects a 
decline of similar order in December quarter as well and prices are expected to remain elevated. 
For the full year 2026, IDC continues to project a decline of 11.3%, which is on a base of 284 
million computers sold in 2025 that's roughly 30 million decline of computers sold over last year 
and we are not factoring in any growth in computing demand. This is a very sharp decline for 
this industry and it is coming totally in the second half, that's from July to December of 2026. 
 
Now how long does this last? I would rather you hear it from the people who make the 
components and people who make the computers than from me.  
Michael Dell, the founder of Dell Technologies, said in an interview with CNBC on 13th 
October that he expects the memory shortage to get worse next year in terms of demand and 
supply. And that in his own words, it may well be a 4-year problem because there's just not 
enough supply.  
Sanjay Mehrotra, the Chief Executive of Micron, one of the 3 largest memory manufacturers in 
the world, said on its earnings call on 30th September 2026 that Micron expects memory and 
storage supply conditions to be and I quote "much tighter in fiscal year 2027 and 2028 than they 
were in 2026" and it does not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to 
balance.  
SK Hynix, the world's second largest memory manufacturer, reported in its results on 28th of 
October 2026, that's just a few days ago, that DRAM prices rose by a high-twenties percentage 
in a single quarter and NAND by mid-20s percentage. This is the second consecutive quarter of 
increase of that order. The Chief Financial Officer, Kim Woo-hyun, said and I quote "Memory 
supply cannot keep pace with this level of demand and growth" and described the shortfall as a 
constraint projected to continue through 2030. Its Chief Executive, Kwak Noh-jung, said the 
company's DRAM and HBM volumes for the next 3 years through 2029 are effectively sold out. 
 
The simple reading is that the large part of the world's memory capacity is going to AI and the 
personal computer is further back in the queue. This is now fully visible in the price of a new 
computer. A year ago, the sweet spot for a laptop in India was around INR35,000 to INR40,000. 
That same computer today is now between INR65,000 to INR72,000. And here is what that 
means for our customer. 
 
If a new computer costed INR100 earlier, our refurbished premium computer used to cost around 
INR30. We used to peg it at around 30% of a brand-new computer. The gap was INR 70. That

same new computer today costs INR180, which is an 80% increase from last year and ours has 
potential to go to INR54. 
 
If it goes to INR54, the gap will be around INR126. In absolute terms, the saving for the customer 
has almost doubled. And that's what has made the refurbished proposition even stronger. This 
will also allow us to peg our product as a percentage of a brand-new computer much above 30% 
than what we are currently doing. In case of phone or car market, the refurbished phone or car 
are typically sold at 45% to 50% price of a new car or a new phone. So this is a huge opportunity 
for us.  
What does this do to customer behavior? When the cost of a new technology rises, the 
conversation naturally shifts from ownership to access, value and usability. For a business, a 
college or a student, they still need a computer. The need has not gone anywhere, but they are 
now asking a different set of questions. Does every requirement need a brand-new device? Can 
the useful life of a good device be extended? How do I get reliable computing without putting 
more pressure on my budget? 
 
This is where we believe professionally refurbished devices have an increasingly important role 
to play, and it is what Electronics Bazaar has been built to offer, a premium refurbished device 
that works like new, looks like new and comes with a credible warranty of one to three years at 
a fraction of the price of new. 
 
The story for Electronics Bazaar refurbished computer is only starting.  
Having said all that, I want to be very clear on one point because I know that it's on your mind. 
Every time a new computer gets more expensive, the case for Electronics Bazaar gets stronger. 
But our case was strong before and it will be strong after. Elevated memory prices are a near-
term catalyst for us. They are not the foundation of our business. Our long-term growth is not 
dependent on the memory price cycle, and we believe the refurbished PC market will continue 
to expand even if memory prices moderate because what is driving it is a structural shift towards 
affordability, reliability and sustainability. 
 
Let me explain why we say that. On affordability, even before the shortage, we price a premium 
refurbished device at around 30% of the price of new. That gap does not close when memory 
prices moderate. And should memory prices correct someday, never say never, we have a big 
cushion. Our significant inventory is sourced at old prices. And because the absolute saving for 
the customer is now far greater, we can peg our product at a higher share of the new prices than 
before. In cars and phone, as I just said, pre-owned sells at 40% to 50% of new. We are at 30%.  
On reliability, the hesitation that once surrounded refurbished has reduced because of product 
quality, a 1- to 3-year warranty and a buying experience customers can rely on. That is trust built 
over time.  
On sustainability, enterprises and governments are increasingly asked to extend the life of what 
they own and to reduce e-waste and a professionally refurbished device answers both.

Management Commentary
3
“We delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY27, with Revenue, EBITDA and PAT registering year-on-year growth of 59.2%, 30.5% and 25.4% 
(H1 FY27 as 61.9%,28.9%, and 23.7%) respectively. This performance was supported by healthy volume growth of 14.4% YoY (H1 FY27 growth 
as 18.7%) and disciplined cost management . EBITDA per kg for Q2 FY27 improved to Rs. 12.6 (H1 FY27 as 12.5) , reflecting the resilience of our 
business model amid metals price volatility.
Our extensive global procurement network of over 1,000 scrap yards, long-standing supplier partnerships and increasing focus on domestic 
sourcing enable us to secure quality raw materials at competitive prices. Further strengthening our sourcing strategy is a structured LME-
linked hedging framework, complemented by customer price pass-through mechanisms. Together, these measures help us manage 
commodity price exposure effectively and maintain margin stability.
Our integrated manufacturing capabilities, specialised alloy development, advanced technology and pioneering liquid metal supply model 
set us apart in the industry. Long qualification cycles, just-in-time deliveries and deep customer integration foster strong customer 
relationships and create meaningful entry barriers. These strengths position CMR as a strategic supplier to leading OEMs and Tier-I vendors.
The recent one notch upgrade in our credit ratings by CRISIL to AA-/Stable for long-term facilities and A1+ for short-term facilities reflects 
our strengthened financial standing and enhances our financial flexibility to support future growth.
As we enter the next phase of sustainable growth, our focus remains on expanding capacity, strengthening our presence in non-automotive 
segments by scaling our billets, sheet ingots and UBC recycling businesses. By enhancing our product mix, driving operational efficiencies 
and maintaining capital discipline, we aim to sustain healthy margins and reinforce our leadership in recycled aluminium and other non-
ferrous metals, while creating enduring value for our stakeholders.”
-
Mr. Mohan Agarwal
Chairman & Managing Director
CMR Green Technologies Ltd

Management Commentary
3
“We delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY27, with Revenue, EBITDA and PAT registering year-on-year growth of 59.2%, 30.5% and 25.4% 
(H1 FY27 as 61.9%,28.9%, and 23.7%) respectively. This performance was supported by healthy volume growth of 14.4% YoY (H1 FY27 growth 
as 18.7%) and disciplined cost management . EBITDA per kg for Q2 FY27 improved to Rs. 12.6 (H1 FY27 as 12.5) , reflecting the resilience of our 
business model amid metals price volatility.
Our extensive global procurement network of over 1,000 scrap yards, long-standing supplier partnerships and increasing focus on domestic 
sourcing enable us to secure quality raw materials at competitive prices. Further strengthening our sourcing strategy is a structured LME-
linked hedging framework, complemented by customer price pass-through mechanisms. Together, these measures help us manage 
commodity price exposure effectively and maintain margin stability.
Our integrated manufacturing capabilities, specialised alloy development, advanced technology and pioneering liquid metal supply model 
set us apart in the industry. Long qualification cycles, just-in-time deliveries and deep customer integration foster strong customer 
relationships and create meaningful entry barriers. These strengths position CMR as a strategic supplier to leading OEMs and Tier-I vendors.
The recent one notch upgrade in our credit ratings by CRISIL to AA-/Stable for long-term facilities and A1+ for short-term facilities reflects 
our strengthened financial standing and enhances our financial flexibility to support future growth.
As we enter the next phase of sustainable growth, our focus remains on expanding capacity, strengthening our presence in non-automotive 
segments by scaling our billets, sheet ingots and UBC recycling businesses. By enhancing our product mix, driving operational efficiencies 
and maintaining capital discipline, we aim to sustain healthy margins and reinforce our leadership in recycled aluminium and other non-
ferrous metals, while creating enduring value for our stakeholders.”
-
Mr. Mohan Agarwal
